skill.name: figma
skill.description: Import Figma assets, tokens, components, motion context, shaders, and storyboards into HyperFrames compositions. Use it when a user provides a Figma link.
skill.summary: Bring Figma design material into HyperFrames as local assets, tokens, components, and motion guidance.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown examples or prose references, not Ruby backtick execution. The audit keeps credential handling and telemetry-related command execution for review because the skill asks agents to inspect or persist Figma tokens and run npx event commands. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Do not ask agents to inspect project .env files. Direct users to configure read-only tokens outside the repo or in approved secret storage.
Remove advice to persist personal access tokens in a project .env unless the file is ignored and the user explicitly approves it.
Make event reporting opt-in at runtime, document data sent, and avoid npx execution when a local trusted binary is unavailable.
Add explicit escaping guidance for Figma URLs and require confirmation before running CLI commands with user-provided input.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable ways to move Figma designs into HyperFrames without manual asset tracking. This skill routes assets, tokens, components, motion, shaders, and storyboards through the right import path.
actual_capabilities: Routes Figma links to asset, token, component, motion, shader, or storyboard workflows.
Guides HyperFrames CLI imports for local assets, brand tokens, and components.
Explains how to freeze imported files locally with provenance for deterministic renders.
Maps Figma motion context into supported timeline guidance for GSAP output.
Describes storyboard reconstruction from keyframes, element chains, and director notes.
Identifies shader limitations and directs users toward native Figma exports when needed.
limitations: Requires HyperFrames tooling and a Figma read token for REST-based imports.
Motion and shader workflows depend on Figma MCP access and plan limits.
Cannot access Figma files unless the connected account has permission.
Complex shaders may need a manual Figma export before import.

use_cases.title: Prepare production assets
use_cases.description: Import logos, images, and frame exports from Figma into local HyperFrames media folders.

use_cases.title: Build brand variables
use_cases.description: Pull Figma variables or published styles into HyperFrames brand tokens before component import.

use_cases.title: Reconstruct motion storyboards
use_cases.description: Turn storyboard frames and director notes into element timelines instead of flat slide sequences.

prompt_templates.title: Import one asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Import this Figma frame into my HyperFrames composition as a local asset. Prefer SVG for vector artwork: <Figma link>

prompt_templates.title: Pull brand tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Figma file to import brand colors and styles into HyperFrames variables. Tell me which tokens were added: <Figma file link>

prompt_templates.title: Create a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an editable HyperFrames component from this Figma frame. Link fills to imported tokens when exact bindings exist: <Figma frame link>

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild a storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Figma storyboard section as animation keyframes. Reconstruct element motion, use notes below frames, and freeze final assets locally: <Figma section link>

output_examples.input: A logo frame link and a request to add it to an intro composition.
output_examples.output: The skill chooses the asset workflow, freezes the logo locally, records provenance, and reports the media path and next preview step.

output_examples.input: A design system file with colors and typography styles.
output_examples.output: The skill imports available tokens or published styles, then explains which variables should be added to the composition.

output_examples.input: A storyboard section with several frames and motion notes under the strip.
output_examples.output: The skill treats frames as keyframes, matches repeated elements, applies director notes, and identifies scenes that need component import.

best_practices: Use read-only Figma token scopes and keep tokens out of prompts and committed files.
Import tokens before components so component colors can link to brand variables.
Freeze Figma assets locally before rendering so output does not depend on live Figma access.
anti_patterns: Do not paste personal access tokens into chat or commit project environment files.
Do not treat storyboard frames as slides when repeated elements should animate over time.
Do not leave live Figma URLs as runtime dependencies inside the final composition.

faq.question: Does this skill write to Figma?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only imports and local HyperFrames output.

faq.question: Does it need a Figma token?
faq.answer: Yes for REST imports. The token should use read-only scopes only.

faq.question: Can it import Figma motion?
faq.answer: Yes, when Figma MCP motion context is available for the selected file and node.

faq.question: What happens to shaders?
faq.answer: Shader support is limited. The workflow usually asks for a native Figma export.

faq.question: Where are imported assets stored?
faq.answer: The workflow freezes assets locally and records provenance for deterministic rendering.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
